study.question: Does the useful transported full-task Q pivot bit require the original auxiliary-to-click row correspondence, or can a bit from permuted auxiliary cotangent triples reproduce the click-AUC effect at the same forward architecture and native transfer radius/support?
study.hypothesis: Local observation: g3-r0063 full-task negative/positive AUCs are0.6689610675617089/0.6683760511656333, while cart+buy negative/positive are0.6683238588338976/0.668814448433831. Fav-only negative/positive in g3-r0062 are0.6688025544975889/0.6687481637940922. The source-by-sign pattern suggests that the all-task bit carries conditional correspondence information that a task subset does not preserve, but these single-seed results do not establish that mechanism. Provisional mechanism hypothesis: retaining auxiliary/click row alignment when constructing Q provides a useful orientation signal beyond auxiliary norm, support and a generic state-dependent sign. Replace only the bit-construction cotangents by an occupied half-batch permutation, crossing both external signs to distinguish source dependence from a simple sign convention. The radius, line and old gates continue to use native full-task cotangents. A surrogate VJP is explicitly used; the scalar joint BCE is not its potential function.

nearest_work.difference: Closest exact local source, SHA256 c67a6408b02fffc06e145350cbeb41236a58a7b84555ed1cf5818e2385c27889. Keep the fixed-angle line/radius/gates and full-task bridge expression; add only a second bit source made from permuted auxiliary cotangent triples.

Earlier source replacement removes fav only from bit construction. This replacement keeps all three tasks and their joint occupied-row cotangent multiset, but breaks their original alignment with click K within eligible pairs.

Earlier control reassigns the actual O transfer and reprojects its geometry. Here reassignment acts only inside a scalar bit helper; the real transfer line, radius and support remain native at a fixed state.
Earlier rolled labels train the whole auxiliary objective differently and degrade auxiliary predictions. Here all true-label losses and private gradients stay ordinary; only the bit source changes.

Resolved primary version and read lines245-284; local target-aware unnormalized activation and BCE are inherited adaptations. DIN does not verify this auxiliary surrogate. No exact DIN reproduction or priority claim.

Read cached primary benchmark section2.3, lines1-39. The fifteen architecture descriptions are alternative forward interaction designs; this round changes only training-time bit sourcing. Original-method full texts and gradient-method priority are not verified.

inherited_components: The entire g3-r0063 negative full-task bridge Model and true-label training_loss, including context collection and private gradient gates.
DIN-style unnormalized target activation, authorized item/action embeddings, compressed history and inherited task-specific matching/order representations.
The rank16 context-history product adapters and fixed-angle nuisance-line canonicalization from the local successful lineage.
Existing FP64 centered click/auxiliary components, half-batch reassignment, tangent helper, coordinate carriers, pivot convention and old support gates.
All earlier task-subset/constant/click-bit helpers still execute equally in all four cells; no new modules, parameters, buffers, RNG calls or inference work.
study.proposed_difference: Before constructing a replacement Q sign, set donor_j=roll(j,B/2) only where both rows have histories; otherwise retain the original row. Apply the same involutive permutation to each of the three auxiliary context cotangents after FP64 conversion. Recompute C/O, reassigned O and tangent Q with the original click cotangent and mask fixed. Extract its first-max-absolute pivot bit, exact-zero ->+1. Multiply the native canonical fixed-angle transfer by this bit and the chosen external sign. Do not substitute donor radius/line/validity or alter the native bridge expression. The full 2x2 source-by-sign design is implemented as four standalone modules with common helper work.
predictions: Fixed-state: all cells give identical predictions, state updates and private-task gradients. Native bridges replay g3-r0063 negative0.6689610675617089 and positive0.6683760511656333 before source interpretation, under the same deterministic host conditions.

At a fixed state, donor/native transfer masks and radii agree exactly up to FP64/cast rounding; their vectors differ only by a global sign on bit-disagreement batches. Eligible permutation is bijective on occupied rows and preserves complete auxiliary triples.

Directional prediction: native negative click AUC exceeds donor negative. The native negative-minus-positive contrast exceeds the donor negative-minus-positive contrast if original correspondence supplies the advantageous signed signal.

The correspondence contrast is informative only if the donor helper frequently changes the bit; report eligible-row fraction, bit agreement and sign balance together with Q zero/near-zero/tie rates. No disagreement makes the intervention weak rather than falsifying the mechanism.

Parameter count is expected to remain32192421 (31793216 embeddings,399205 dense), inferred from unchanged definitions. Inference work is unchanged; training adds one source-bit reconstruction in every arm, so measure its overhead rather than claim efficiency.
falsifiers: If meaningful bit disagreement occurs and donor negative matches or improves native negative, the directional correspondence-benefit hypothesis fails in this single-seed setting; if donor also reproduces the source-by-sign contrast, original mapping is unnecessary for that observed effect.
If a donor orientation equals or outperforms the best native orientation, do not claim original alignment is required for achieving that click AUC, even if the prespecified interaction changes.
Any forward/state/private-gradient difference at identical weights, changed actual radius/support, invalid tensor geometry or failed native replay invalidates a bit-only causal interpretation.
A reversal or vanishing contrast in later host-authorized paired seeds would refute robustness. A replay at the identical seed cannot supply repeated statistical support.
A click improvement alone does not establish broad multi-task quality, sparse parameter-space gradient alignment, label semantics, production-time validity or novelty.
alternative_explanations: The permuted objects are feature/probability/label-dependent cotangents, not labels. Donors are not guaranteed independent users; no raw user IDs are available to the model.
The half-batch pairing also enters the inherited Q construction. This prespecified deterministic pairing is not representative of all possible permutations.
Only pairs with two occupied histories exchange. Full auxiliary information remains in transfer norm, validity and the learning trajectory.
Changing an early bit changes later model states, radius, gates and private gradients; only fixed-state local comparisons isolate the bit.
Canonical pivot sign depends on coordinate order and can change at near ties. Global row-space orthogonality need not survive cast, shared-ID accumulation, clipping or adaptive optimization.
Many validation-driven branches and one frozen seed make new full-validation comparisons exploratory. Replays are determinism checks, not independent repetitions.

Generic sign scheduling, pivot instability or adaptive-optimizer trajectories may explain the effect. Cotangent pairing can preserve or manufacture batch structure, and inherited norm/gates still carry auxiliary information.

Historical weak/abandoned branches include buy-only context0.6673203922314733, rolled auxiliary objective0.6674639465810746, FP32 aggregate collection0.6674397049498135 and reassigned-negative O0.6680188315050506. They are distinct interventions at different lineage points, not matched controls here. Bit removal0.6687531802698141 and click-bit0.6687444859805948 approach the incumbent, leaving the specificity of the auxiliary bit uncertain.
The incumbent improves click relative to DIN but has lower auxiliary AUCs (approximately0.8104/0.8256/0.8029 versus DIN0.8491/0.8649/0.8702); click selection does not establish a Pareto improvement.

The supplied trajectory index contains no non-success status and previous_runtime_error is null. Unavailable local tensor/validator interfaces are missing prerequisites, not failed mechanism experiments. Earlier unknown campaigns are not evidence.
